records.claim: Birth defects can happen in any pregnancy for different reasons. Out of all babies born each year, about 3 out of 100 (3%) will have a birth defect. We look at research studies to try to understand if an exposure, like venlafaxine, might increase the chance of birth defects in a pregnancy. While some studies suggest that taking venlafaxine during pregnancy could possibly increase the chance of birth defects, several large studies have not found a higher chance of birth defects. If there is an increased chance of birth defects above the background risk with use of venlafaxine in pregnancy, it is likely to be small.
